title: Deliver the product as a Manifest V3 Chrome extension built in TypeScript with a content script and service worker
decision: Build the product as a Chrome extension on Manifest V3, written in TypeScript, with no UI framework: a content script performs DOM traversal and selector-based extraction of the question and answer option text from the active tab and applies highlight styling by injecting a single extension-owned CSS class on matched answer elements, while a service worker coordinates activation and writes diagnostic log entries to extension-local persistent storage surfaced through the Chrome extensions page. AI provider integration, AI response parsing, and the test harness remain unresolved and are not selected here.
rationale: The SRS fixes the delivery vehicle: the product must be installable and operable as a Chrome extension inside the student's browser, triggered from the browser's extension controls, operating on the quiz page as displayed in the student's tab without a separate application or window (R-9), and it must read the question and answer options from the displayed page content itself (R-4) and apply styling-only indication to answer elements on that page (R-11, R-3). A Manifest V3 extension with a content script is the only shape that satisfies all of these at once: the content script is the mechanism that touches the page DOM for extraction and class-based styling, and the service worker is the mechanism that survives page navigation to keep logs retrievable after the quiz page is closed and reopened (R-7). TypeScript is chosen because the failure contract is strict and silent (R-5, R-6, R-8): every AI response, extraction result, and threshold decision must be handled without surfacing anything to the screen, so typed boundaries around the extraction output, the model-assigned per-answer probabilities, and the highlight decision reduce the chance of an unhandled path that would either throw visibly or highlight on a malformed value. No UI framework is used because the product must add no window, panel, overlay, text, or label to the page (R-3, R-11) and must leave the page visually unchanged on every failure (R-5, R-6); a framework would add rendering surface with no requirement to justify it. The founder register decision for empty and first-use states is implemented directly by this architecture: the content script treats any page whose extracted content does not match the expected question-and-answer structure as a no-op, producing no probabilities and no highlight and writing only to the extension-local log, which is how the extension does nothing when the page data is not what it expected while remaining as non-intrusive as possible. The 80% inclusive threshold is applied as a fixed comparison against the model-assigned per-answer probability with no product-side recomputation, calibration, or adjustment (R-12, R-11).

options_considered.option: A standalone web application the student opens in a separate browser window alongside the quiz
options_considered.reason: Rejected: it violates the requirement that highlighting appear on the quiz page itself with no separate page, window, or panel (R-2, R-3) and that the product operate without the student opening a separate application or window (R-9).

options_considered.option: A browser userscript installed through a userscript manager
options_considered.reason: Rejected: it is not installed through the browser's own extension installation mechanism nor listed among installed extensions (R-9), and it gives no extension-owned persistent log surface retrievable through the extensions page (R-7).

options_considered.option: A Manifest V3 extension with a framework-based UI layer rendering a results panel
options_considered.reason: Rejected: any rendered panel, overlay, or added text is prohibited (R-3, R-11), and the added rendering surface increases the risk of a visible artifact on failure (R-5, R-6, R-8) with no requirement that needs it.

options_considered.option: A Manifest V3 extension written in plain JavaScript without static typing
options_considered.reason: Rejected: the silent-failure contract (R-5, R-6, R-8) depends on exhaustively handling malformed extraction and model output, and untyped boundaries make an unhandled path that throws or mis-highlights more likely.
